shared_qualifications: C1: source Fig.6 composition is at% Mo, with Al balance in the stated binary alloy. Using CIAAW Al26.982 andMo95.95 (https://ciaaw.org/abridged-atomic-weights.htm), wt%Mo=100*x*95.95/((100-x)*26.982+x*95.95). Inverting original CRA binary wt% cells gives approximately2.8,5.4,10.4,3.0,4.0,5.0,6.0 and8.2 at% Mo forCRA720-727, respectively. These are explicitly dataset-derived calculations, not independent paper composition measurements.

The actual enlarged Fig.6 points and original registry coordinates are retained; the smooth fitted line is not an observation. Crowded points near3-6 at% are distinct specimens. Matching only a similar potential would conceal composition conflicts. Plausible alternatives around5.0/5.4 at% are retained without choosing the closest potential.

obs_004 at approximately4.0 at% Mo has about-145 mV(SCE), whereasCRA724 corresponds to approximately4.0 at% but says-330 mV. Composition/medium independently support the identity, with discrepant potential agreement; no reassignment to a nearby-330 mV marker is made. obs_003/005/006/007/008/010 have unresolved composition-counterpart differences and remain candidates.

The binary films were RF magnetron sputter-deposited and contain Mo in solid solution (PDF pp.2-4). Source0.1 N KCl is N2-deaerated and adjusted topH8 withKOH. For monovalent KCl,0.1 N supplies0.1 mol/L chloride. Source sweep rate is0.2 mV/s after OCP change<1 mV over6 min; the CRA scan-rate cell is blank, not zero.

All source potentials use SCE, so no electrode offset is applied. Source methods do not establish numerical25/26 C test temperatures in the inspected passages; CRA temperature values are not copied to the paper side. The Al-13Mo no-degradation limit at0 V has no corresponding13 at% CRA material and is not treated as a measured breakdown.
Poppler returned success with Symbol/ArialNarrow font warnings. The relevant source text, axes, markers and captions were legible, including the enlarged Fig.6.
